findings.title: failure_taxonomy has no ids for scheduler conservation or refresh-service liveness
findings.detail: The taxonomy covers timing (TIMING_*), protocol state (PROTO_*), refresh state (REF_*), init, data and CSR failures, but a queue+arbiter can also drop an enqueued request, issue a command that matches no request, or never service a refresh request — and none of those has an id. Validation checks these today under proposed local ids and requests their adoption into the spec: SCHED_001 (enqueued request never issued as a command), SCHED_002 (command issued matching no enqueued request), SCHED_003 (refresh request raised but never serviced with a REFRESH command). Declared in Validation/gates/stage_invariant_rules.json under proposed_taxonomy_extensions.

findings.title: failure_taxonomy has no ids for init/calibration ordering, refresh-versus-init ordering, or a tREFI interval violation
findings.detail: Bringing the six autonomous paths (init -> calibration, init -> refresh, and the four status-reporting paths) under real checks needed failure classes the taxonomy cannot name. INIT_001/INIT_002 cover mode-register order and inter-step timing, but not: init_done raised before the sequence completed (INIT_003); calibration finishing before init_done (CAL_001); periodic ZQCS requested before cal_done (CAL_002); a refresh requested before init_done (REF_003); no refresh ever requested after init_done (REF_004). Separately, every timing parameter in timing_model has a TIMING_* id except tREFI — a MAXIMUM interval rather than a minimum separation — so the refresh-interval assertion reports under a proposed TIMING_012. Checkers and assertions use these ids locally; adoption into the spec is requested. The intake gate (Validation/spec/spec_completeness.py, rule TAXONOMY_NAMES_TIMING_PARAMS) now flags an unnamed timing parameter on arrival.
